Eddy County North Dakota Inmate Lookup

If you need to locate an inmate in Eddy County, North Dakota, there are several official resources available to help you find current information about individuals in custody. An eddy county north dakota inmate lookup can be performed through the county sheriff's office, state corrections department, and local court systems. This guide walks you through the process and provides you with the tools and information you need to access inmate records quickly and efficiently.

How to Search Eddy County Jail Records

  1. Start with the Eddy County Sheriff's Office inmate search database, which maintains records of individuals currently held in the county jail facility.
  2. Visit the North Dakota Department of Corrections website if the inmate may have been transferred to a state facility or sentenced to state custody.
  3. Gather basic information about the person you are looking for, including their full name, date of birth, or case number, as this will speed up your search considerably.
  4. Enter the information into the appropriate search tool and review the results, which typically display booking information, charges, and custody status.
  5. Contact the Eddy County Sheriff's Office directly by phone if you cannot locate the person through online databases or need additional information.
  6. Check court records if you need details about charges, court dates, or case status, as these are public documents in North Dakota.
  7. Keep in mind that it may take several hours after arrest before an inmate appears in the searchable database due to booking procedures.

Bail Bond Information for Eddy County

If an inmate has been arrested in Eddy County, bail or bond may be set at their initial arraignment hearing. Most bail bondsmen in the area charge a 10% non-refundable fee of the total bond amount, which is the standard rate across North Dakota. For example, if bond is set at $5,000, you would pay $500 to the bondsman, and they would post the full amount to secure the inmate's release. This fee covers the bondsman's risk and administrative costs and is not returned even if the charges are later dismissed.

The arraignment typically occurs within 24 to 72 hours of arrest, and this is when the judge determines if bail will be granted and at what amount. Bail decisions depend on factors such as the severity of charges, the inmate's prior criminal history, ties to the community, and whether they pose a flight risk. If you cannot afford a bail bondsman, you may request a public defender and discuss alternative release options with the court, such as unsecured bond or release on your own recognizance.

Visitation Rules at Eddy County Jail

  • Identification Required: All visitors must present a valid government-issued photo ID before entering the facility.
  • Visitation Hours: Contact the Eddy County Sheriff's Office for current visiting hours, as schedules may vary based on facility operations and security needs.
  • Dress Code: Visitors must dress appropriately; clothing should cover the torso and upper legs, with no transparent or offensive materials.
  • Video Visitation: Remote video visitation options may be available for those unable to visit in person; inquire with the facility for scheduling details.
  • Children's Policy: Children under 18 may be allowed to visit with parental supervision, but check facility rules first, as restrictions may apply.
  • No Contraband: Visitors cannot bring any items into the jail, including cell phones, weapons, drugs, or unauthorized materials.
  • Visitation Duration: Visits are typically limited to 30 minutes to one hour, depending on facility capacity and security protocols.

What to Expect After Arrest in Eddy County

  1. Booking Process: When an individual is arrested, they are transported to the Eddy County Jail for booking, where personal information, charges, and identifying details are recorded in the system.
  2. Medical and Safety Screening: All newly booked inmates undergo a medical evaluation and screening to assess immediate health needs and any safety concerns.
  3. Classification and Housing Assignment: Inmates are classified based on the severity of charges, custody level, and other factors to determine appropriate housing assignments within the facility.
  4. Initial Appearance and Arraignment: Within 24 to 72 hours, the inmate is brought before a judge for their initial appearance, where charges are read, rights are explained, and bail is determined.
  5. Transfer to Other Facilities: If an inmate is sentenced to state custody or transferred to another jurisdiction, they may be moved to the North Dakota State Penitentiary or another facility.
